subject: Security questionnaire kick-off & SOC 2 / HIPAA clarification for HealthQuant
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Sokolov <elena.sokolov@healthquant.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + next steps on security intake (SOC 2 / HIPAA)

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Helpful to hear how HealthQuant plans to use Redwood for secure model inference in your analytics pipeline. Short recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Scope: inference-only (no storage of PHI on our hosted service). You mentioned some endpoints will process tokenized patient identifiers for de-duplication; need to confirm data classification for those flows.
- Compliance signals requested: SOC 2 Type II report, HIPAA controls (BAA conversation), and your standard vendor SIG/CAIQ questionnaire.
- Timeline: you’d like a preliminary answer on major gaps by next Tues (2026-12-22).

To move forward, can you please: 
1) Send the completed SIG Lite or your CAIQ export if you have one (we can prefill where possible).
2) Confirm whether the data processed will be PHI as defined under HIPAA (a simple yes/no is fine).
3) Indicate any required evidence artifacts (e.g., pen-test report, SOC 2 attestation, vulnerability scanning reports) and preferred delivery method (SFTP/Drive/Portal).

Marissa (security ops) — looping you in to lead the prefill and any follow-up evidence requests. Monica — FYI on timeline and SOC 2 artifact.

Best,
Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — short SOC 2 highlights]

From: Elena Sokolov <elena.sokolov@healthquant.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Greg Turner <greg.turner@healthquant.com>, security@healthquant.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on security intake (SOC 2 / HIPAA)

Thanks Aditya — appreciated the summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PHI: yes, some payloads will include PHI fields (patient IDs and partial demographic tokens). We will need a signed BAA before onboarding any PHI flow.
- SIG: attaching our vendor intake form (HealthQuant_SIG_Request_v1.pdf). It's the short version of our SIG — we expect the vendor to prefill where possible and return supporting docs for high-risk items.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II (last 12 months) is required. We also ask for recent external pentest (last 18 months) if available.
- Data residency: US-only for this use case.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 
A) Sign a BAA and route keys so PHI never persists on shared storage?
B) Provide SOC 2 report and pen-test evidence to our secure upload (link below) by 2026-12-22?

I’ve uploaded the SIG form as an attachment to this thread.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of IT Security | HealthQuant
[attachment: HealthQuant_SIG_Request_v1.pdf (PDF, form)]

---
HealthQuant Secure Upload: https://uploads.healthquant.com/secure/abc123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Sokolov <elena.sokolov@healthquant.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 12:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on security intake (SOC 2 / HIPAA)

Elena — thanks for the SIG and the upload link. Quick technical clarifications from SecOps so we can prefill accurately: 

1) BAA/PHI handling: Redwood can execute a BAA. Our hosted offering will be configured with customer-isolated keying and no persistent PHI storage by default for this deployment pattern; we will document the configuration in the evidence bundle.

2) SOC 2: we will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II attestation (neutral-coverage exceptions noted in the report). High-level: encryption-in-transit and at-rest, role-based access controls, logging/monitoring with 90-day retention in the UI and 1 year exportable logs. I will attach the SOC 2 summary to the bundle.

3) Pen-test: We have an external penetration test from Q1 2026; full report redacted for third-party IP will be provided where allowed. If HealthQuant requires the unredacted version, we'll coordinate an NDA-specific transfer.

SIG clarifying questions (to help prefill):
- Under "Data Classification": should we mark PHI as "high" and note partial tokenization in the comments?
- Under "Subprocessors": do you need the full list or only those with access to live inference infrastructure?
- Under "Encryption Key Management": do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for production? (We can support both customer-managed and Redwood-managed keys; which is preferred?)

Next steps I propose:
- We will prefill the SIG with responses for the controllable items and send a redline back by EOD Monday (2026-12-21).
- Deliverables to HealthQuant secure upload by Tue 2026-12-22: SOC 2 attestation (PDF), pen-test summary (redacted PDF), prefilled SIG form.

If you confirm the KMS preference and data-classification labeling, we’ll incorporate it into the prefill.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Security Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)]

From: Elena Sokolov <elena.sokolov@healthquant.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Greg Turner <greg.turner@healthquant.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps on security intake (SOC 2 / HIPAA)

Marissa — great, thanks for the clear plan. Quick answers below so you can proceed with the prefill: 

- Data classification: mark PHI as "high" and add a note: "partial tokenization applied to identifiers; full PHI elements redacted prior to storage". That matches our internal classification.
- Subprocessors: we need the full current list; if you expect changes in the next 6 months, please note the update cadence and notification policy.
- Key management: we prefer customer-managed KMS for production. For initial integration testing a Redwood-managed key is acceptable provided we have an upgrade path to KMS before go-live.

We can accept redacted pen-test reports. I confirm HealthQuant secure upload is the delivery channel; please include manifest with SHA256 checksums.

I’ll look for the prefilled SIG and artifacts by Monday. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena
Head of IT Security | HealthQuant
